definitions.explanation: A large marine mammal that breathes air through blowholes. Whales have significant cultural and historical importance in Japan.

examples.japanese: {船|ふね}から{鯨|くじら}が{潮|しお}を{吹|ふ}くのが{見|み}えた。
examples.english: We could see a whale spouting water from the boat.

examples.japanese: {鯨|くじら}は{海|うみ}で{最|もっと}も{大|おお}きな{動物|どうぶつ}だ。
examples.english: Whales are the largest animals in the ocean.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}の{頃|ころ}は{給食|きゅうしょく}に{鯨|くじら}の{肉|にく}が{出|で}ることがあった。
examples.english: When I was a child, whale meat was sometimes served in school lunches.

notes:
{鯨|くじら} refers to whales in general.

Common expressions:
- {鯨|くじら}{肉|にく} (whale meat)
- {鯨|くじら}{油|あぶら} (whale oil)
- {捕鯨|ほげい} (whaling)
- {鯨|くじら}を{飲|の}む (to swallow a whale - to do something impossible)

Types of whales:
- シロナガス{鯨|くじら} (blue whale)
- ザトウ{鯨|くじら} (humpback whale)
- マッコウ{鯨|くじら} (sperm whale)

Counter: {頭|とう}

Cultural note:
Whale meat has been consumed in Japan for centuries, and some coastal towns have whale festivals. However, international controversy over whaling has made this a sensitive topic. Many younger Japanese have never eaten whale meat.
